capture.diag.notExcluded.en: our app is not in SCShareableContent — per-app exclusion is not in effect (pid %1$d)

capture.hint.adhoc.en:
It can be denied even when System Settings shows it on — this app is ad-hoc
signed, so rebuilding changes the signature, and TCC ties the grant to the old one.
  tccutil reset ScreenCapture %1$@
then start it again and allow. Running ./tools/make-signing-cert.sh once removes
this round trip for good.

capture.problem.notStarted.en: capture did not start. Screen Recording permission appears to be granted.

capture.problem.stopped.en: capture stopped and has not come back. The screen is unshaded until it does.
capture.problem.stopped.note: Shown in the menu bar after a stream has been down for 30 seconds. The app keeps trying to reopen it.

check.motionGates.en: %1$@set these to 0 to turn it off: %2$@
check.motionGates.note:
%1$@ is the slot number when there is a chain ("2. "). With only one it is the
empty string, so it has to sit inside the indent for the line to stay aligned.

cli.alreadyRunning.en:
global-shader is already running%1$@.

A second instance films the first one's overlay — SCContentFilter excludes by
process, so the same app is not excluded from its own capture. The shader then
runs over its own output every frame and the screen falls apart.

If you meant to change the shader, just name the file — the running one changes:
  global-shader <shader.frag>
  global-shader --profile <name>

To stop it: ◲ → Quit in the menu bar, or
  global-shader --stop
cli.alreadyRunning.note:
%1$@ is either " (pid 123)" or the empty string. The pid cannot always be found,
so the parentheses go in and out with it.

cli.err.setNeedsArgs.en: --set needs a name and a value

cli.usage.en:
global-shader — put a fragment shader over the whole screen.

  global-shader                      start with the chain saved in the settings
  global-shader <shader> [<shader>…] apply in the given order and save that chain
  global-shader --profile <name>     apply a profile

If one is already running, all three **change the running one and exit.** A second
instance is never started — that would be feedback in itself.

Options (this run only. The menu bar is where you change things for good)
  --fps N          capture/render cap. Defaults to each display's refresh rate.
  --scale F        capture/render resolution scale (0.25–1.0). The first knob to
                   reach for when frames run short. Pixel count falls as F² —
                   0.8 drops 36% of them.
  --no-hot-reload  do not re-read a shader when its file changes.
  --redraw M       keep drawing even when the screen does not change.
                   auto | always | never. auto turns it on when any shader in
                   the chain reads time.
  --diag           feedback diagnostic. Draws a marker in the top-left 64px and
                   watches for it in the next capture. If it comes back, the
                   overlay is filming itself.
  --exit-after N   exit on its own after N seconds.
  --capturable     let the overlay appear in screenshots and screen recordings.
  --allow-multiple skip the instance lock. **Feedback will run.** For testing.
  --no-knobs       do not promote `#define NAME value  // @min..max` to uniforms.
  --no-vsync       turn off vsync. For measuring what a shader really costs.
  --space-fix M    how to handle the stale frame right after a Space switch.
                   off | freeze | hide.
  --lang L         language for this run. Otherwise the settings, then the system.
  --check          translate and build the pipeline only. No window, no permission.
  --dump-msl       --check plus the translated MSL on stdout.

Talking to a running instance (unix socket)
  --get            every knob as JSON (in a chain, ids look like "2.CURVE")
  --set NAME VAL   change one knob. On a name clash, qualify it as "2.CURVE".
  --reset [NAME]   go back to the values in the shader file
  --chain          the current chain as JSON
  --profiles       the saved profile names
  --reload         re-read the shaders
  --status         the current state as JSON
  --stop           exit
  -h, --help
  -V, --version

Everything spoken over the socket is always English. It is a hole for programs,
not for people, so the answer must not depend on a language setting.

Settings live in ~/.config/global-shader/config.json, profiles beside it in profiles/.

Shader conventions (both are detected automatically)
  hyprland    v_texcoord / tex / screen_size / pointer_position / time inside main()
  shadertoy   iChannel0 / iResolution / iTime / iMouse inside
              mainImage(out vec4, in vec2)

To stop it: Quit from the menu bar status item, or SIGINT/SIGTERM to this process.
cli.usage.note:
Everything -h prints. One key per block rather than per line, because the column
alignment of the option descriptions differs by language.

dlg.chooseShaderFolder.en: A folder with shaders in it

dlg.loginItemFailed.en: Could not change the login item

log.allowMultipleNoSocket.en: --allow-multiple: not opening the control socket (it belongs to the running instance)

log.captureReopened.note: %1$@ is a display name. Logged when a stream that the system ended comes back.

log.controlSocketFailed.en: could not open the control socket: %1$@

log.feedbackNo.en: → no feedback. the overlay is excluded from capture.

log.feedbackYes.en: → feedback is running. the overlay is not excluded from capture.

log.needPermission.en: Screen Recording permission is required. System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen Recording.

log.woke.note: Logged on the wake notification, before the streams are reopened.

login.err.managedByNix.en: %1$@ is managed by Nix. Turn it on and off there.

menu.capturable.tip.en: On, the shader appears in screenshots. In exchange another capture tool can feed our output back.

menu.fps.tip.en: The cap for capture and render. Lower it to save battery.

menu.hotReload.tip.en: Re-read a file in the chain when it changes.

menu.knobPromotion.tip.en: Promotes #define with an @range comment to a uniform so you can move it live. Measured cost is zero.

menu.language.tip.en: The menu changes right away. Lines already printed to the log stay in the language they were written in.

menu.loginItem.managed.tip.en:
%1$@
It cannot be changed here. Turn it on and off where it is declared.

menu.mayBeDenied.en: it can be denied even when the box is checked

menu.mayBeDenied.tip.en:
This app is ad-hoc signed, so rebuilding changes the signature. TCC ties the grant to the old one, so the entry stays and only the access is denied.

  tccutil reset ScreenCapture %1$@

then start it again and allow. Running tools/make-signing-cert.sh once removes this round trip.

menu.redraw.tip.en: Auto looks at whether the shader reads time. The battery cost only applies when it is on.

menu.resetPass.en: This pass back to file values

menu.saveProfileAs.en: Save the current one as a profile…

menu.scale.tip.en: The first knob to reach for when frames run short. Pixel count falls with the square of the scale.

menu.shaderDirHint.en: add one under Settings → Shader folders

menu.spaceFix.tip.en: What to do when capture hands over a stale frame right after a switch.

renderer.err.noPipeline.en: could not find main0, or could not build the pipeline

shader.demoted.en:
promoting knobs breaks compilation; loaded without them.

shader.err.toolMissing.en:
%1$@ not found. Install it and build again:
    brew install glslang spirv-cross
    nix shell nixpkgs#glslang nixpkgs#spirv-cross -c ./build.sh
shader.err.toolMissing.note:
When a tool was not found. All three routes are given — there is no telling whether
Homebrew or nix is in use.
